Actionstep is a pioneer in the development and sale of software-as-a-service (SaaS) products, specializing in the delivery of Legal Practice Management and Legal Accounting software. We are a fast-growing, dynamic business with a global customer base of more than 50,000 and a team of over 250 across the USA, Australia, UK, Canada, and New Zealand. 
 Actionstep is expanding its product portfolio and adding richer AI functionality across the platform to deepen customer value, accelerate cross-sell revenue, and introduce new add-on modules that increase competitive differentiation. 
 THE PURPOSE OF YOUR ROLE 
 The Strategic Finance Analyst is a core contributor to Actionstep’s Finance team. The role’s initial focus areas are core FP&A work, including forecasting and profitability analysis; gross margin and pricing analysis; and commission calculations across Sales, Partner, and Operations teams. You will report to the VP of Finance and work closely with the broader Finance and RevOps teams. As Actionstep’s needs evolve, the specific mix of responsibilities may shift, and you may take on additional or different analytical work over time. 
 ABOUT YOU 
 You are a strong finance analyst who thinks in numbers first, and you’re just as comfortable in the data and systems behind those numbers as you are in a spreadsheet. You build clean, reliable models and analysis, and you understand that the work behind a recurring deliverable has to be right every time, not most of the time. 
 You bring real curiosity to the business behind the numbers. You do not just produce an analysis, you ask what it means and whether it should change how the business plans or decides.  
 You move comfortably between recurring, deadline-driven deliverables and more open-ended strategic analysis, and you know how to prioritize when both compete for your time. 
 You build trust across Finance and other teams by being accurate, responsive, and clear about what your analysis does and does not say. You take feedback well and ask questions up front rather than guessing. 
 WHAT YOU WILL BE DOING 
 The focus areas below reflect the business’s current priorities. As with most roles on a growing team, they may change as those priorities evolve, and may also include support for strategic initiatives such as partnerships or M&A as they arise. 
 FP&A: Forecasting & Profitability 
 Support the development and maintenance of annual budgets and rolling forecasts. 
 Conduct budget-to-actual variance analysis and support profitability analysis across the business. 
 Build and maintain financial models to support business decisions, including scenario and sensitivity analysis, particularly through the use of AI tools. 
 Contribute datasets and analysis to board and executive reporting materials. Work closely with other members of the Finance team, including the Senior Financial & Systems Analyst, on shared data and reporting priorities. 
 Pricing & Gross Margin Analysis 
 Conduct gross margin analysis by product, segment, and customer cohort, and identify trends and margin improvement opportunities. 
 Support pricing strategy and annual price increase analysis, including modeling impact across customer segments, for new and existing product lines. 
 Partner with Billing and RevOps to validate pricing and margin data before it reaches leadership. 
 Commission Calculations 
 Support monthly/quarterly commission calculations for Sales, Partner, and Operations teams, including quality control checks prior to distribution. 
 Partner with Sales, RevOps, and Partner teams to ensure the data behind commission calculations, such as bookings, quotas, and contract terms, is accurate. 
 Investigate and resolve commission discrepancies as they arise. 
 Data & Systems 
 Partner with the Senior Financial & Systems Analyst on the data and systems behind the company’s business intelligence, recurring reporting, and general analysis efforts. 
 Automate recurring deliverables, such as commission calculations, to reduce manual, spreadsheet-based work over time. 
 Contribute to the infrastructure work, the “plumbing,” that keeps Finance’s data and systems running reliably via a company-wide data warehouse. 
 Help document the business logic behind recurring Finance calculations so it’s repeatable and scalable. 
 Build or maintain dashboards and reporting views that support recurring Finance deliverables. 
 Flag data quality issues upstream and work with the relevant team to fix them at the source.  
 EXPERIENCE & QUALIFICATIONS 
 Required 
 Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field. 
 1–3 years of proven work experience as a Financial Analyst, or in a similar FP&A, accounting, or business analysis role. 
 Strong Excel skills, including advanced formulas and financial modeling. 
 Working knowledge of SQL and curiosity to learn more. 
 Excellent analytical skills and comfort working with large, sometimes imperfect datasets. 
 Ability to present financial data clearly through reports, charts, and summaries for both financial and non-financial audiences. 
 Hands-on experience with financial or ERP systems. 
 Strong personal accountability for accuracy, particularly on recurring deliverables that affect employee pay. 
 Preferred 
 Experience in a SaaS or subscription-based business. 
 Experience with NetSuite or a similar ERP platform. 
 Experience with a cloud data warehouse platform (e.g., Snowflake) or BI/reporting tools (e.g., Power BI). 
 Prior experience with sales commission calculations, gross margin analysis, or pricing analysis. 
 THIS ROLE REPORTS TO 
 VP of Finance (Christian Ebersol). 
 METRICS OF SUCCESS 
 Accuracy & reliability: recurring deliverables are accurate and delivered on time, with minimal rework. 
 Analytical value: your analysis is trusted and used by Finance leadership and cross-functional partners in decision-making. 
 Cross-functional trust: partner teams across the business view Finance as a reliable, responsive partner. 
 Growth in scope: demonstrates readiness to take on broader financial planning and strategic analysis responsibilities within 12 to 18 months. 
 Medical, dental, vision offerings
 RRSB with company match
 Flexible working and PTO
 Take your birthday off
 Frequent team-building events 
 Fantastic training and development opportunities

 A Propos du poste: 
 Joignez-vous au Groupe Edelweiss à titre de Spécialiste junior, Ressources humaines et systèmes dans un rôle qui soutient les activités de ressources humaines pour l’ensemble du Groupe.
 Vous serez la principale personne responsable de notre système d’information sur les ressources humaines (SIRH) ainsi que le principal point de contact à cet égard. Vous offrirez également un soutien pratique lors des intégrations RH lorsque de nouvelles entreprises se joignent au Groupe, notamment pour l’intégration de nouvelles entités au SIRH et le déploiement des politiques. Vous agirez aussi comme ressource généraliste au quotidien, selon les besoins du Groupe.
 Vous contribuerez également à repérer et à mettre en place des automatisations simples, y compris des solutions assistées par l’intelligence artificielle, afin de rendre les intégrations et les tâches administratives courantes en RH plus rapides et moins manuelles.
 Comme la composition des entités du Groupe, les territoires de compétence et les priorités évoluent constamment, ce poste convient à une personne véritablement curieuse, qui sait s’adapter à un environnement en constante évolution, plutôt qu’à une personne recherchant une routine fixe et un rôle étroitement défini.
 Le candidat retenu sera basé à Montréal et travaillera dans notre bureau à Saint-Laurent. 
 Vos responsabilités: 
 Soutien au intégrations du SIRH 
 Soutenir la personne responsable des RH du Groupe dans l’intégration des entreprises nouvellement acquises aux systèmes du Groupe Edelweiss, notamment en transmettant les renseignements sur les employés dans le SIRH, en veillant à leur exactitude et en assurant l’intégrité des données relatives aux profils, aux dossiers et à la documentation des employés pendant les intégrations.
 Animer des séances d’apprentissage en direct portant sur la formation aux nouveaux systèmes et aux systèmes existants auprès des équipes nouvellement intégrées.
 Soutien aux systèmes et automatisation par l'IA 
 Développer et maintenir une connaissance approfondie des capacités, des fonctionnalités, de la structure, de l’entretien et de la logique des flux de travail de la plateforme SIRH, afin de résoudre les problèmes, de soutenir les utilisateurs finaux et d’orienter les décisions de configuration.
 Repérer les possibilités d’automatiser les tâches administratives et d’intégration RH répétitives à l’aide d’outils d’intelligence artificielle et des fonctionnalités de flux de travail du SIRH, notamment les communications et la validation des données.
 Créer et maintenir des automatisations simples à l’aide d’outils assistés par l’IA, de formules ou de macros Excel, ou encore des outils de création de flux de travail du SIRH, afin de réduire la saisie manuelle de données et les efforts liés à la production de rapports.
 Soutien administratif aux ressources humaines 
 Contribuer à l’élaboration et à la mise en œuvre de politiques, de procédures et de programmes de ressources humaines visant à améliorer l’expérience employé au sein des entreprises du portefeuille du Groupe.

 Fournir un soutien administratif général selon l’évolution des priorités du Groupe, notamment en matière de conformité, de recrutement, d’intégration et de départ des employés, ainsi que dans le cadre de projets ponctuels.

 Diplôme collégial ou baccalauréat en ressources humaines, en administration des affaires ou dans un domaine connexe; une expérience équivalente sera également considérée.
 Au moins deux ans d’expérience en administration et en coordination des ressources humaines, ainsi qu’une expérience avec des systèmes SIRH.
 Capacité démontrée à s’adapter rapidement à des situations nouvelles, inconnues ou changeantes, puisque la combinaison d’entités, de territoires de compétence et de priorités associée à ce poste évolue constamment.
 Aisance ou intérêt marqué pour les systèmes SIRH, comme BambooHR, et les technologies générales liées aux ressources humaines.
 Curiosité sincère à l’égard des outils d’intelligence artificielle et aisance à les utiliser pour améliorer la productivité quotidienne et les processus.
 Excellente maîtrise de l’environnement Microsoft Office, particulièrement Excel.
 Aptitudes techniques et capacité à apprendre et à adopter rapidement de nouvelles technologies et de nouveaux systèmes.
 Excellentes compétences organisationnelles et grand souci du détail, ainsi que capacité à gérer plusieurs priorités concurrentes dans le cadre de projets d’intégration et du soutien quotidien en ressources humaines.
 Volonté d’apprentissage continu et excellentes aptitudes pour établir et entretenir des relations professionnelles.
 Excellentes aptitudes en communication écrite et orale, ainsi que de bonnes compétences en présentation.
 Bilinguisme en français et en anglais.
 Atouts: 
 Expérience ou exposition aux intégrations en ressources humaines dans un contexte de fusions et acquisitions.
 Expérience en analyse de données.
 Connaissance des lois du travail et des exigences de conformité dans plusieurs pays.

 À titre de Spécialiste junior , Ressources humaines , vous jouerez un rôle central dans l’intégration harmonieuse des entreprises nouvellement acquises au Groupe Edelweiss, tout en soutenant les besoins en ressources humaines à l’échelle du portefeuille, au fur et à mesure qu’ils se présentent.
 Votre capacité d’adaptation contribuera au bon déroulement des intégrations et des activités RH quotidiennes, même lorsque les priorités changent. Votre curiosité à l’égard de l’intelligence artificielle et de l’automatisation aidera également le Groupe à améliorer continuellement ses façons de travailler.
 Votre contribution aura une incidence directe sur l’expérience employé et sur le succès global du Groupe Edelweiss.

About Faire 
 Faire is a technology wholesale platform built on the belief that the future is local. Independent retailers around the globe collectively represent a multi-hundred-billion-dollar wholesale market that has historically been fragmented and offline. At Faire, we're using the power of tech, data, and machine learning to connect this thriving community of entrepreneurs across the globe. Picture your favorite boutique in town — we help them discover the best products from around the world to sell in their stores. With the right tools and insights, we believe that we can level the playing field so businesses can grow and local communities can thrive.
 We’re looking for smart, resourceful and passionate people to join us as we power the shop local movement. If you believe in community, come join ours.
 Role Overview
 Faire’s marketing org runs largely on systems marketing does not currently build. Audiences and attributes, campaign automation, landing pages, attribution, translation, paid feeds, monitoring and alerting: today most of it gets assembled request by request, or waits on a partner engineering pod carrying its own roadmap. The Marketing Engineer builds those systems inside marketing, on Faire’s production stack, and enables marketers to then run solo.
 This is an engineering role sitting inside marketing. You will write production code across Faire’s codebase, own services end to end, take part in on-call, and put agents into marketing workflows with the evals and monitoring that make them trustworthy at scale. You will be measured on whether the marketing org gained a capability it did not have before.
 The surface you own can span various disciplines: Paid media tooling and feed automation, the landing page framework, lifecycle and campaign systems, the marketing data layer, internal platform tooling, and the consumption layer for Faire’s recommendation and propensity models inside marketing surfaces are all in scope. You will help define how we work with our broader EPDD partner teams.
 What you'll build first
 Before you join, these problems will probably have moved, you should be comfortable with that. Below are two current problems we’re looking at solving short term:
 Marketing-led landing pages. Our current marketing led landing pages workflow is slower than it should be for the blog, newsroom and content teams, and for landing page tests in lifecycle and paid we’re often spending more time talking/prioritizing experiments than building experiences for them. You will own this surface end to end, and you will own the recommendation on where it goes next: you might decide between vendor vs. in-house solution, or build a self-serve, agentic landing page service. The outcome is simple, better, faster landing pages, more self serve, and happy partner teams.
 Self-serve audiences and attributes. Our partner teams currently go through us for Audience syncing with paid platforms and marketing led lifecycle. We think this should be a self service capability available to our marketers: whether that's a vendor or in-house, how the data contract gets enforced in code, and what the self-serve layer looks like are all open questions this person will answer to ensure we reach the right person at the right time with the right message.
 Other projects on our radar: a learning loop for generative assets in ad campaigns, improving infra behind core intelligence feeds powering our paid campaigns, real-time recommendation management across lifecycle and paid, and more.
 How we work
 Own services end to end. Design, build, review, deploy, monitor.
 Ship in Faire's production codebase, to Faire's engineering standards, with code review by engineers.
 Sit with lifecycle, paid, brand and product marketing rather than behind a ticket queue. Find the pattern behind the requests, then decide what to build so they stop arriving.
 Put agents into the patterned majority of the queue, with an eval harness, monitoring and a defined failure mode before anything reaches a customer.
 Turn ambiguous asks into a scoped, prioritized plan, and communicate tradeoffs and progress to non-technical stakeholders.
 Qualifications
 Required
 4+ years shipping and owning production software, in or adjacent to a marketing, growth or GTM organization.
 You'll work in Faire's production codebase. Faire’s stack is Kotlin, Java, JUnit, Hibernate, Guice and Jersey, React and Next.js, HTTP, JSON and Protocol Buffers, MySQL and CockroachDB, on AWS.
 SQL and enough comfort in the warehouse to instrument what matters and decide what to build next from the data.
 Depth in at least one marketing platform: a CDP or ESP (Braze, Iterable, Segment, Hightouch), an attribution or analytics platform, a CMS, or an ad platform API.
 Daily use of AI coding agents, plus experience putting LLMs into production systems with evals, monitoring and a defined failure mode.
 A track record of owning a system end to end, including the on-call, and shipping it to non-technical users who then operated it without you.
 Preferred
 Marketplace or two-sided e-commerce experience.
 Production experience with Kotlin or Java on the backend and JavaScript or TypeScript with React or Next.js on the frontend.
 Having replaced a martech vendor with an in-house build, and being able to say what it cost.
 Braze, Hightouch, Google Ads, Meta.
 Salary Range 
 Toronto: the pay range for this role is $140,000 to $192,500 per year. 
 This role will also be eligible for equity and benefits. Actual base pay will be determined based on permissible factors such as transferable skills, work experience, market demands, and primary work location. The base pay range provided is subject to change and may be modified in the future.

Additionally, hybrid in-office roles will have the flexibility to work remotely up to 4 weeks per year. Specific Workplace and Information Technology positions may require onsite attendance 5 days per week as will be indicated in the job posting. 
 Why you’ll love working at Faire 
 Move fast: You'll own meaningful problems that serve customers around the globe with the agency to move fast and see your results clearly.
 Equipped to scale: We invest in what matters, including the latest enterprise AI tools, to help you work smarter and get more out of every day.
 Best in class: Our team is full of sharp, kind, and generous colleagues who care about their craft and about helping you grow in yours.
 Real rewards. Competitive pay, equity, and comprehensive benefits designed to support your life inside and outside of work.
 Belonging: We're intentional about building an environment where every Faire employee has equal access to opportunities, growth, and success.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who is obsessed with customer success, takes the responsibility of durably storing customer data seriously, and has strong empathy for both their team and our users.
 This role can be based remotely in Ontario, Canada.
 About the Storage Execution team
 The Storage Execution team sits at the heart of MongoDB’s Online Transaction Processing (OLTP) team. We own the core transactional read/write path on each node, across both today’s storage engine and a next‑generation cloud-native storage architecture. Our work determines how correct and performant MongoDB is for customers running mission-critical production workloads.
 The team’s responsibilities include:
 Defining and maintaining the internal collection and index APIs used by Replication, Query and Catalog modules, and commands for local reads and writes, plus the transaction and durability primitives that govern visibility, conflict resolution and crash recovery
 Integrating the next generation of MongoDB’s storage architecture into the server in a way that is predictable for other teams, scales with cloud elasticity, and preserves the performance and safety of the classic configuration
 Improving transaction processing speed and semantics of both single shard and cross-shard transactions
 Owning index builds and schema‑level storage operations (build/rebuild, cleanup, resumability) and ensuring they behave well for large, highly available clusters running write-heavy workloads
 Building validation, diagnostics, and storage‑focused test infrastructure to catch durability issues early and keep the system trustworthy at scale
 Partnering with neighboring teams on flow control, prioritization and load-shedding to stay within resource limits, protecting durability and availability at the cluster level without starving critical operations

 Lead, grow and manage a New York–based team of 8 to 10 engineers; ensure clear expectations, high standards, and healthy, sustainable execution

 Partner closely with Replication, Query, Sharding, Catalog & Routing, Storage Engines, and Atlas teams on cross‑team features such as the new storage architecture, availability improvements, and workload management
 Represent Storage Execution in planning, staffing, and calibration; make thoughtful tradeoffs between near‑term deliverables, longer‑term availability gaps, and platform investments

 Demonstrated customer obsession: direct experience working with demanding customers (or customer support / cloud teams) on complex incidents and turning them into clear, outcome‑oriented recommendations

The Saint John Board of Police Commissioners (the “Commission”) is seeking a forward-looking police leader to serve as its next Chief of Police.
 Reporting to and receiving direction from the Commission, the Chief of Police serves as the Chief Executive Officer of the Police Force and the senior law enforcement leader for the community.
 The Chief will lead a police service focused on effective, lawful, ethical and community-centred policing. You will provide visible leadership across the organization, champion public trust and community partnerships, and connect the Commission’s strategic direction to the decisions and actions of members across the Force.
 As Chief, you will lead and administer the Force in accordance with the Police Act, provincial policing standards, Commission policies and the Commission’s strategic direction. You will be accountable for organizational performance, professional conduct, public confidence and community safety outcomes.
 The Role
 As Chief of Police, you will maintain an effective, transparent working relationship with the Commission and comply with its lawful direction and instructions. You will develop, implement and oversee professional police procedures and ensure members carry out their duties professionally, fairly and in compliance with applicable law, standards, policies and collective agreements.
 You will report regularly to the Commission on operations, organizational performance, progress against the strategic plan, policy compliance, risks, emerging issues and matters requiring Commission awareness or action. You will maintain accountability for the performance, conduct, professionalism and communications of the Force and its members.
 In leading the Force, you will:
 ·   Champion an inclusive community policing service-delivery model built on public trust, community partnerships and problem solving, grounded in the principle that “police are the public and the public are police.”
 ·   Create and sustain an inclusive, participatory working environment for sworn and civilian members, full- and part-time employees, contract workers and volunteers.
 ·   Provide visible leadership across the organization so members understand strategic priorities and how their decisions and actions contribute to community safety and well-being.
 ·   Promote a culture of openness to new ideas, creativity, innovation, teamwork, learning, accountability and continuous improvement.
 ·   Convey a positive and credible image of the Police Force to the public, community partners, stakeholders and media.
 ·   Model integrity, authenticity, transparency, professionalism, fairness and respect in all decisions, communications and relationships.
 Organizational Leadership
 You will manage and direct the Police Force to meet or exceed applicable policing standards while taking into account local conditions, evolving risks and community expectations.
 You will prepare and propose annual budget options to the Commission, identifying anticipated operational impacts and alignment with strategic priorities and objectives. You will directly supervise, develop and mentor Deputy Chief(s), senior leaders and other direct reports, sworn and civilian.
 You will establish and oversee fair, unbiased and transparent systems for hiring, development, supervision, evaluation, recognition, compensation, promotion and discipline. You will prepare the organization for the future through succession planning and the ongoing development of middle and senior managers.
 You will build and maintain constructive relationships with labour associations, municipal partners, community organizations, partner agencies, provincial bodies and policing counterparts. You will also participate in the City’s Public Safety Committee meetings.
 The Ideal Candidate
 You are an experienced and respected police executive who understands the opportunities and challenges of leading a small or medium-sized police service. Ideally, you have served as a Chief of Police or Deputy Chief, or held a comparable senior executive leadership role, within a small or medium-sized Canadian municipal police service or detachment.
 You understand that leadership in a police service in a regional city requires both strategic perspective and a visible, hands-on leadership presence. You are comfortable working directly with the Commission, senior leaders, members of the Force, municipal partners, labour associations, community organizations and other policing and public-safety partners.
 You have demonstrated your ability to work with partners to reduce crime, improve community safety and well-being, and respond to complex public-safety challenges. You have successfully managed in a unionized environment and bring experience with large operational budgets, financial planning and controls, procurement, resource allocation, and related financial and administrative responsibilities.
 You have a proven record of building trust within diverse communities and across all ranks and employee groups within a police organization. You are a visible and credible leader who communicates effectively, develops people and builds strong organizational teams.
 You understand modern independent civilian police governance and oversight, including the Commission’s role as employer, supervisor and strategic governance body. You know how to build an effective relationship with a civilian police commission while respecting the distinct responsibilities and accountabilities of the Chief and the Commission.
 You are comfortable navigating uncertainty and taking accountability for matters you can influence, not only those you directly control. You bring adaptive leadership, systems thinking and complex problem-solving skills, together with an inclusive orientation, empathy, innovation and a commitment to continuous improvement.
 You will bring the judgement and leadership experience to guide the Force through its next chapter while maintaining the trust of its members, the Commission and the community it serves.
 Working in the Community
  The Chief works primarily in an office and meeting environment and regularly attends Commission meetings, internal meetings, public events, community forums and partner-agency engagements.
 As Chief, you will maintain a visible and accessible presence with members of the Force, community partners and the public. You will maintain required police qualifications and may travel outside the jurisdiction for professional meetings, networking and related duties.
 The Chief is expected to reside locally and to be available for significant operational, public-safety or organizational matters as required.
 You will ideally bring post-secondary education in a field relevant to policing, community safety and well-being, public administration, leadership, law, criminology or a related discipline.
 Experience leading organizational transformation, equity-focused initiatives, community partnerships and modern police-service delivery is also preferred.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

Why this role?

We are on a mission to build machines that understand the world and make them safely accessible to all. Data quality is foundational to this process. Machines (or Large Language Models, to be exact) learn in similar ways to humans, by way of feedback. By labelling, ranking, auditing, and correcting model output, you will improve Large Language Models' performance for iterations to come, thus having a lasting impact on Cohere's technology. We are hiring Generalist professionals with broad backgrounds that span multiple consumer-facing or personal domains.

This is a judgment-driven role, not passive data entry. You will review, assess, and provide structured feedback across a broad and evolving range of tasks, evaluating, stress-testing, and improving our models on English-language data spanning multiple modalities (text, image, and structured formats such as JSON, CSV/TSV, and Markdown). This is a great opportunity for professionals with strong analytical skills to contribute to high-impact annotation projects.

Please Note: This is a part-time independent contractor position available within Canada only. We seek candidates who can commit to 16 hours per week at a CAD $30/hour contract rate. This role is BYOD 💻 (Bring Your Own Device, laptop). This position is remote.

As an Data Annotation Specialist, you will:

 - Evaluate and rank model outputs: Complete preference and comparison tasks, assessing which responses best conform to project guidelines for accuracy, helpfulness, tone, and safety, and writing clear justifications for your judgments.

 - Stress-test and break models: Probe models adversarially to surface failure modes, unsafe behavior, and capability gaps, and document reproducible cases that engineering and research teams can act on.

 - Create datasets: Author high-quality prompts, responses, and exemplars to build training and evaluation datasets, following detailed specifications and editing machine-written or human-written outputs to standard.

 - Build and apply rubrics and taxonomies: Contribute to the design of grading criteria and rubrics, then apply them consistently to produce structured, high-quality annotations across task types.

 - Annotate and correct multimodal data: Label, audit, and rectify inaccuracies across text, image, and structured data, maintaining a high standard of data integrity and accuracy.

 - Calibrate and maintain consistency: Participate in calibration exercises and inter-annotator agreement checks to align on standards, and flag ambiguous or uncovered edge cases rather than guessing, since a single misjudgment replicated at scale degrades a model.

 - Adapt to experimental work: Take on new and evolving task types as project needs shift, applying sound judgment in areas where guidelines are still being developed.

 - Report on model performance: Surface and communicate quality and performance trends in model and agent behavior, giving cross-functional partners clear, well-evidenced feedback on where models succeed, fail, and degrade.

You may be a good fit if you have:

 - 1+ years of experience in AI data annotation, LLM evaluation, content moderation, research, or a related analytical role, with exposure to quality assurance, and/or preference ranking.

 - Experience applying detailed guidelines to complex and often ambiguous content, with strong contextual and sociocultural judgment, sensitivity to nuance, tone, and register, and the ability to reason well in cases where there is no single correct answer.

 - Comfort with ambiguity: a willingness to flag unclear or uncovered edge cases rather than guess, and to work productively on novel, experimental tasks whose definitions are still evolving.

 - A sharp, curious eye for inconsistencies, subtle errors, and model failure modes, including the instinct to probe models adversarially and surface where they break. Familiarity with how large language models behave, such as hallucination, sycophancy, and instruction-following gaps, is a plus.

 - Excellent command of written English and strong reading comprehension, with the ability to clearly justify your evaluations, including why an output is correct or incorrect, high-quality or low-quality, and to write clear prompts and exemplars that explain your reasoning. Bonus points if you are fluent in another language!

 - Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy, with the ability to maintain consistency across high-volume and monotonous tasks.

 - Comfort working with annotation platforms and structured formats such as JSON, CSV/TSV, Markdown, XML, and YAML.

 - Strong execution in a remote environment, including good time management, comfort using new tools, and the ability to work independently in a global, asynchronous team.

Candidate Journey

 - Initial Screening: Our Talent Team will review your application.

 - First Assessment: If selected to move forward, you’ll receive a multiple-choice assessment by email.

 - Second Assessment: Candidates who achieve a passing score will be contacted by a member of our team to complete a more comprehensive assessment focused on their area of expertise.

 - Video Screen: If selected to move forward, you’ll have a short video call with a member of our Operations Team.

 - Final: Selected candidates will receive an Independent Contractor Agreement.

As an independent contractor, you maintain control over how you complete your work and may work with multiple clients simultaneously, although we ask you to declare if any of these are with a direct competitor of Cohere and maintain IP confidentiality of the Cohere project. Independent contractors are not eligible for health benefits or other benefits provided to employees. Compensation for services is provided to contractors by contractors invoicing for services provided pursuant to the terms of our agreement with the contractor.

It is important to understand that as an independent contractor, continuous work is not guaranteed. The client-contractor relationship is fundamentally project-based, meaning engagements may be temporary, periodic, or intermittent based on our organizational needs and project availability. As an independent contractor, you should anticipate fluctuations in workflow and, therefore, compensation for services when Cohere does not require as many hours of services in a week.

Prospective candidates, please be advised: this role involves working with human-generated and model-generated tasks that may involve exposure to not safe for work (NSFW) text content as part of data annotation tasks, including explicit, offensive, or other inappropriate material.
